subject.title: BUG: Workboard cannot spawn ACP workers (opencode / Codex / Claude Code)

question: Should Workboard officially support ACP-backed card workers, and if so should it do so through a generic plugin runtime-dispatch seam rather than a Workboard-specific direct call to ACP spawning?
rationale: Current main has no runtime-selection contract, while Workboard's embedded worker path owns card lifecycle semantics that ACP spawning does not automatically prove equivalent to. Choosing the supported capability, defaults, and ownership boundary is a maintainer product and architecture decision.

options.title: Add a generic worker-runtime seam
options.body: Approve a Workboard-owned runtime abstraction with an ACP adapter only after it can preserve card claims, worker callbacks, completion state, and diagnostics.

options.title: Keep Workboard embedded-only
options.body: Retain the current embedded-subagent contract and close the request as an unsupported orchestration mode if maintainers do not want ACP workers in Workboard.

options.title: Externalize the orchestration feature
options.body: Prefer a separately maintained plugin once a sufficient runtime-dispatch extension point exists, keeping bundled Workboard focused on its current embedded worker contract.

recommendation.title: Add a generic worker-runtime seam
recommendation.body: Approve a Workboard-owned runtime abstraction with an ACP adapter only after it can preserve card claims, worker callbacks, completion state, and diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Workboard lifecycle work makes RomneyDa the best available owner for the Workboard-side API and lifecycle decision.
